correctness.rationale: Every factor at length 3^k belongs to a prefix-padded or suffix-padded C_k family because 11 is absent from the block-type sequence. The length-two scattered counts are equivalent to the pair (#1, sum of their positions), injective within each family. For r from 22n/27 through 24n/27, its explicitly matched reflected prefix u=46n/27-r has identical moments; the words differ in their last-one positions by 2n/27>0. The n/27 divisibility and k>=3 are essential. The claimed integer counts follow from an inclusive interval. Finite checker is supporting, not a proof for all k.

Neither cyclic-rotation classes, ordinary Parikh vectors, 2-Abelian classes nor the unrestricted binary 2-binomial partition determine these restricted fibers. The sharp two-family moment argument and explicit centroid collision pairing supply the missing implications.

value.rationale: This is a natural inverse problem for order-two scattered-subsequence statistics on the canonical ternary Cantor automatic word. The theorem establishes uniform two-to-one rigidity *and* an explicit positive linear number of different ambiguous observations over infinitely many scales, a substantive contrast not implied by the known 2-Abelian factor complexity or a generic 2-binomial signature formula. It does not claim an unproved exact census.
